title: Retreat of the Republic of China government to Taiwan
summary: After defeat by the Communists on the mainland, the Nationalist government of the Republic of China moved its seat to Taipei in December 1949, with Chiang Kai-shek flying from Chengdu on 10 December. Taiwan became the base of the Republic of China while the People's Republic held the mainland.

uncertainty.note: Taipei Times dates the announcement of the move to 7 December and Chiang Kai-shek leaving Chengdu for Taiwan to 10 December; other accounts give 8 or 9 December for the relocation. The span covers 7 to 10 December.

where.historical_name: Taipei, Taiwan Province, Republic of China

importance.justification: Fixed the lasting division between the Republic of China on Taiwan and the People's Republic of China on the mainland.

related.because: Nationalist defeat in the civil war and the founding of the PRC left Taiwan as the remaining base of the Republic of China government.

reviewer_note: Least sure of the day: Taipei Times gives 7 December (announcement) and 10 December (Chiang leaves Chengdu); other accounts say 8 or 9 December, which I could not confirm on an opened page. The record uses a 7-10 December span. The pin is Taipei, the seat adopted. Numbers of people who relocated are disputed (about 1 million to 2.5 million per Taipei Times 2016).

beats.caption: Taipei Times dates the announcement of the Nationalist capital's move to Taipei to 7 December 1949; Chiang left Chengdu three days later.
Chiang Kai-shek boarded a plane at Chengdu bound for Taiwan on 10 December 1949, as the retreat from the mainland neared its end.
Estimates of people who relocated to Taiwan in 1948-1950 range from about one million to 2.5 million, making Taiwan the Nationalist base.
